newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-SENIOR DUELS WITH ALKER TO WIN NSW CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SENIOR DUELS WITH ALKER TO WIN NSW CHALLENGE.

text.p: Australian golfer Peter Senior on Sunday duelled with New Zealand's Steve Alker over four play-off holes before winning the New South Wales Challenge and a place in this year's British Open.

Alker equalled the course record with a final round of 65 to force the play-off, which Senior won with a two-metre birdie putt on their fourth sudden-death trip to the 18th hole at the par-72 Terrey Hills course.
Senior had led by two strokes overnight before Alker staged his remarkable final round charge, which included eight birdies, for both players to finish on 14-under 274.
Defending champion Senior lost his lead with a disastrous double-bogey seven at the ninth hole, where his second shot landed in a clump of trees.
That saw Senior fall three shots behind Alker, with Australian Masters champion Peter Lonard and fellow Australian Robert Allenby also vying for the lead.
Senior jumped from fourth into second place on the Australasian PGA Tour Order of Merit to guarantee himself a place in July's British Open at Royal Troon.
With the top three from the Australasian Order of Merit winning exemptions into the British Open, Senior needed to win the season-ending tournament to book a place at Royal Troon.
Senior leapfrogged New Zealand's Michael Long into second place behind Order of Merit leader Lonard, with world number one Greg Norman pushed back to fourth.

Senior's cause appeared lost when he dropped three shots on his opening nine holes before the stocky Australian fought back with five birdies on the closing nine holes, including a 15-metre putt on the 17th hole, to join Alker on 14-under.
Alker was already in the clubhouse after birdeying the final hole to take the outright lead.
"After nine holes I was wondering whether I could get an earlier flight home," Senior later told reporters.
"To win golf tournaments you have got to have lucky breaks and I think that was it," Senior said of his putt at the 17th.
Allenby led briefly after an eagle at the 14th hole but stumbled with a bogey on the 17th hole before carding a 68 to finish in equal second on 276 with Lonard, who shot a 67.
